svg.title: Service Mesh
svg.desc: Service Mesh. Sidecar proxies plus a control plane: mTLS, retries and traffic shifting without touching app code. Step 1, Calls go through proxies: Orders calls Payments: its sidecar intercepts the call and hands it to Payments' sidecar. Step 2, Control plane configures: The control plane sends endpoints, routes, policy and certificates. If it fails, calls still flow. Step 3, Mutual TLS and policy: The proxies authenticate each other with mutual TLS; policy lets Orders in and answers Web with 403. Step 4, Split traffic and retry: A routing rule splits calls 90/10 between v1 and v2, and the proxy retries a failed call in time.

g.text: Orders calls Payments: its sidecar intercepts the call and hands it to Payments' sidecar.
The control plane sends endpoints, routes, policy and certificates. If it fails, calls still flow.
The proxies authenticate each other with mutual TLS; policy lets Orders in and answers Web with 403.
A routing rule splits calls 90/10 between v1 and v2, and the proxy retries a failed call in time.
unavailable: no new configuration, no new certificates
No mesh code in either app.
Because every call passes a proxy, the mesh can add
mutual TLS · retries · timeouts · load balancing · telemetry
The control plane is not on the request path:
it sends updates, and the proxies handle calls on their own.
anyone else: 403, the app is never called
Every proxy reports the same metrics and traces:
requests, errors and latency for every call.
